provenance.question: can the inverse-OT fit be spent once, as a hard-negative miner, and give a cheap supervised arm the LP's advantage?
provenance.hypothesis_class: c_ij = sum_k theta_k (a_ik - b_jk)^2, theta on the simplex, the same standardised 13 descriptors in every arm
provenance.arms: plain (all negatives), hard_lp (32 negatives by the inverse-OT cost), mixed_lp (32 LP negatives + 32 uniform), hard_self (32 negatives by the supervised arm's own cost -- the control)
provenance.selection: tau per arm on validation pairs from the TRAINING subjects
provenance.solver: negative miner: the relaxed LP (CuPDLPx) or a first supervised fit; deployed arm: torch autograd on a masked cross-entropy, Adam, 600 steps
provenance.metric: geodesic error on the target, normalised by sqrt(surface area) -- identical to the main study
provenance.memory: the masked loss keeps one n x n cost and one n x n bool mask; ~192 MB at n=2000 in float64
